response.raw_output: {"premises":[{"text":"Spinach is widely reputed in popular culture and nutrition writing to be an exceptionally rich dietary source of iron.","premise_type":"empirical-citable","candidate_key":null},{"text":"A nineteenth-century published chemical analysis reported spinach's iron content as roughly ten times the value obtained by later analyses.","premise_type":"empirical-citable","candidate_key":null},{"text":"The tenfold discrepancy in the published spinach iron figure originated from a decimal point being placed one position to the right of its correct location.","premise_type":"empirical-citable","candidate_key":null},{"text":"The inflated spinach iron figure was reproduced in subsequent food composition tables, textbooks, and popular media rather than being corrected before wide circulation.","premise_type":"empirical-citable","candidate_key":null},{"text":"Spinach's measured iron content, about 2 to 3 milligrams per 100 grams fresh weight, is comparable to that of many other leafy vegetables and not exceptional.","premise_type":"empirical-citable","candidate_key":null},{"text":"Spinach's public reputation as an iron-rich food arose from the circulated inflated iron figure rather than from independent observation or promotion.","premise_type":"empirical-citable","candidate_key":null}]}
